block.title: The symbolic executor follows both getopt clamp paths to their join
block.p: The getopt scanner clamps the last nonoption index to the public index. The symbolic executor now runs both branches to their common block, including the four-byte store on the branch that lowers the index. Both paths use the same proof at the join. The executor uses the registers assigned on each path to prove that the caller's protected registers keep their values.

The libio cleanup proof uses the same store rule to overwrite the cancel type in a cleanup buffer. The old contents can be any four bytes. The executor checks ownership and width, then follows the pointer store that links the buffer into the thread's cleanup list. Removing ownership, supplying read-only bytes, or shortening the field to three bytes stopped execution at the first store in separate proof runs.
